newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian bill would let foreigners vote locally.
newsitem.headline: Italian bill would let foreigners vote locally.

text.p: Italy's cabinet on Friday approved a draft bill that would seek to clamp down on a wave of illegal immigration but extend the rights of legal foreign residents, including giving them the vote in city elections.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi told a news conference that the draft bill, which must be passed by parliament to become law, would set a quota on how many immigrants could be allowed into Italy each year. The quota has not yet been fixed.
But Prodi said the draft law would give non-European Union citizens who legally reside in Italy the right to vote in city elections as well as run for city council.
Immigrants who have lived in Italy without regular papers for at least six years will be entitled to receive a permit to stay provided they have not committed a serious crime, he said.
The draft bill looked certain to spark a heated debate in parliament as the hard-right National Alliance (AN) party vowed it would never allow immigrants the right to vote.

Maurizio Gasaparri, a senior AN member, said his party was willing to discuss ways of facilitating the expulsion of immigrants but was "opposed to demagogic norms giving the right to vote to non-EU citizens in city elections".

Italy has recently seen a wave of illegal immigration, the latest hitting the southern island of Lampedusa on Friday when 52 North Africans were taken into police custody after making the crossing by boat.
The immigrants, mostly Moroccan, were to be taken to Sicily where they would receive expulsion orders, police said.
